partB: Which event is a covalent modification rather than noncovalent regulation?

Phosphate transfer creates a new covalent linkage on the protein. ATP binding, chaperone association and the specified dimerization change interactions without necessarily changing chemical connectivity.
What part of ATP is normally transferred by a conventional protein kinase?
The terminal gamma phosphoryl group is transferred, leaving ADP. The alpha and beta phosphates remain on ADP; adenosine is not covalently transferred by a conventional kinase.
Which is the usual acceptor atom of a conventional N-linked glycan?
The asparagine amide nitrogen receives the glycan. Ser/Thr hydroxyl oxygen is a common O-glycan acceptor. N-terminal nitrogen and lysine are acceptors for other modifications.
Which motif is a candidate for conventional eukaryotic N-glycosylation?
The usual sequon is Asn-X-Ser/Thr, with X not proline. The second option lacks Asn; the first contains Pro at X and the fourth lacks Ser/Thr at the third position.
What is the canonical composition of the precursor oligosaccharide transferred from dolichol to an N-glycosylation site?
Three glucose, nine mannose and two N-acetylglucosamine residues make fourteen sugars. Replacing GlcNAc with GalNAc or changing the relative glucose and mannose counts produces the wrong composition.
Which enzyme transfers a preassembled oligosaccharide to an ER-luminal protein?
Oligosaccharyltransferase catalyses the N-glycan transfer. O-GlcNAcase removes intracellular O-GlcNAc; kinase and methyltransferase transfer different groups.
Which statement about O-GlcNAc is correct?
It is always a complex extracellular glycan
It is attached to asparagine by OST
It requires a transmembrane helix in the target
It can cycle on cytosolic Ser/Thr through OGT and OGA
OGT adds a single GlcNAc to appropriate hydroxyl groups and OGA removes it. It does not require conventional ER N-glycosylation or a transmembrane helix.
Which common modification neutralizes the usual positive charge of lysine?
Acetylation forms a neutral amide at the lysine side chain. Trimethyllysine remains positively charged, and the other modifications affect different residues.
Which donor is normally used for protein methylation?
SAM transfers methyl groups and becomes S-adenosylhomocysteine. ATP, UDP-glucose and myristoyl-CoA are donors in different chemical reactions.
Use of SAM as a methyl donor
Sirtuins use NAD+ during deacetylation. Other deacetylase families may instead use metal-dependent hydrolysis. Dolichol, SAM and ubiquitin are unrelated donors in the listed reactions.
Which is the typical acceptor of canonical N-myristoylation?
The free alpha amino group of an N-terminal glycine forms an amide with myristate. An internal glycine is not an N-terminus unless cleavage exposes it.
What linkage commonly joins palmitate to a cysteine side chain?
Typical S-palmitoylation produces a thioester that may be hydrolysed by thioesterases. Prenylation creates a thioether; the other choices describe unrelated chemistry.
Which location is typical of the mature domain of a plasma-membrane GPI-anchored protein?
GPI attachment occurs on the luminal side of the ER; the luminal orientation becomes extracellular at the plasma membrane. Cytosolic lipid anchors have different topology.
Which is an example of limited irreversible maturation?
Proteolytic conversion of proinsulin to insulin
Specific peptide-bond cleavage creates new termini and cannot be simply reversed in the cell. The first and last involve reversible chemical marks, and AMP binding is noncovalent.
Which statement describes common ubiquitin attachment?
Ubiquitin always marks every target for degradation
Ubiquitin transfers a free methyl group
Ubiquitin's C-terminal glycine can join a substrate lysine
The standard bond links ubiquitin's terminal carboxyl group to a substrate lysine amino group. Ubiquitin has additional nondegradative roles; it is not a methyl donor or RNA attachment mechanism.
Which modification can initiate recruitment of a phosphotyrosine-binding SH2 domain?
An SH2 domain recognizes phosphotyrosine in a suitable sequence context. The other modifications may affect interactions but do not supply that phosphotyrosine epitope.
What makes conventional glycosylation distinct from glycation?
Glycosylation is typically enzyme-directed with activated donors
Glycation is a nonenzymatic reaction involving reducing sugars. Glycosylation is generally enzyme-directed; not all glycosylation occurs in the ER, and glycation can modify proteins.
Why is phosphorylation not invariably activating?
Its effect depends on the structure and interactions of the target
The same negatively charged group can stabilize different conformations or change binding in different ways. Glycogen phosphorylase and glycogen synthase illustrate opposing effects.
Which is an example of a modification that can begin before translation terminates?
All glycosylation is prohibited until release
All ubiquitination requires an extracellular protein
N-linked glycosylation of a nascent ER protein
Many N-glycans are transferred as a polypeptide enters the ER. PTM terminology does not mean all modifications wait for termination.
Which statement correctly distinguishes proteolytic processing from protein degradation?
Processing can generate a functional mature product; degradation destroys the original functional protein
Limited cleavage can activate, inactivate or alter a precursor without wholesale destruction. Both processes can use proteases; cleavage is not ordinarily reversed.
Assertion: A phosphatase can remove a protein phosphate. Reason: It typically regenerates ATP from the released phosphate and ADP.
Both true; reason does not explain assertion
Removal is true, but a conventional phosphatase hydrolyses the substrate linkage and releases phosphate rather than regenerating ATP.
Assertion: A cytosolic protein can carry O-linked GlcNAc. Reason: OGT and OGA participate in dynamic intracellular O-GlcNAc cycling.
Both true; reason does not explain assertion
The intracellular enzymes explain how cytosolic substrates can acquire and lose the sugar without entry into the secretory pathway.
Assertion: An Asn-Ala-Thr motif guarantees N-glycosylation in a eukaryotic protein. Reason: Conventional OST acts on the luminal side of the ER.
Both true; reason does not explain assertion
A motif is necessary in the standard example but not sufficient. Correct topology and accessibility are essential, so the reason is true and the assertion is false.
Assertion: Trimethylation and acetylation of lysine have similar nominal mass increases. Reason: Both modifications neutralize the lysine side-chain positive charge.
Both true; reason does not explain assertion
Both give roughly +42 Da, but their exact masses differ. Acetylation neutralizes ordinary lysine charge; trimethyllysine remains positively charged.
Assertion: GPI anchoring and prenylation can promote membrane association. Reason: GPI anchors are typically attached in the ER lumen, while prenylation commonly acts on cytosolic proteins.
Both true; reason does not explain assertion
Both are true, but the compartment distinction explains orientation rather than the general membrane affinity, which arises from hydrophobic lipid insertion.
NAD+ is required by sirtuins and SAM donates methyl groups. Every other option pairs enzymes with incorrect typical donors.

Which set of statements is correct? I. N-terminal acetylation and lysine acetylation modify different amino groups. II. GPI anchoring involves cleavage of a C-terminal signal region. III. Every ubiquitin mark inevitably leads to degradation.
I and II are correct. III is false: ubiquitination also contributes to sorting and signaling.
Match modification to linkage: 1 N-myristoylation; 2 S-palmitoylation; 3 Cys prenylation; 4 conventional phosphorylation of Ser. a thioether; b phosphomonoester; c amide; d thioester.
Myristate forms an amide at the terminal amine, palmitate a thioester at sulfur, prenyl a thioether at sulfur and phosphate a phosphomonoester at Ser oxygen.
Which combination is correct? I. Endo H cleaves susceptible high-mannose glycans. II. Typical complex N-glycans resist Endo H. III. Endo H releases every O-glycan.
Endo H acts on particular N-glycan structures, including oligomannose and some hybrid forms; it does not remove all O-glycans.
Match the event with its most direct possible outcome.
Mannose-6-phosphate is a targeting tag on many lysosomal enzymes' glycans. Other choices confuse chemically different processes.
partC: A reversible modification has k_add = 0.18 min⁻¹ and k_remove = 0.06 min⁻¹. What steady fraction is modified?
Use f = k_add/(k_add+k_remove) = 0.18/0.24 = 0.75. The unmodified fraction is 0.25; the ratio 0.18/0.06 is not a fraction.
A system has k_add = k_remove = 0.10 min⁻¹. Both constants are doubled. What changes?
Occupancy rises to 1
Occupancy remains 0.5; relaxation half-time halves
Occupancy halves; time unchanged
Both occupancy and relaxation time double
The ratio remains 0.20/0.40 = 0.5, but ln2/(k_add+k_remove) falls from 3.47 to 1.73 minutes. Equal scaling changes flux and dynamics, not the steady fraction.
After complete inhibition of a kinase, a mark decays with a four-minute half-time. From 80% occupancy, what remains after twelve minutes?
Three half-times give 80% × (1/2)^3 = 10%. This assumes fixed total protein and first-order removal without new phosphorylation.
An enzyme has total concentration 2 µM, unmodified turnover 3 s⁻¹ and modified turnover 9 s⁻¹. At f = 0.5, its maximal rate is?
6 µM/s
9 µM/s
18 µM/s
12 µM/s
One micromolar of each form contributes 3 and 9 µM/s, respectively, for 12 µM/s. The total rate requires both concentration and turnover.
Three independent binary sites have occupancies 0.5, 0.6 and 0.2. What fraction carries all three?
Under independence, multiply the site probabilities: 0.5 × 0.6 × 0.2 = 0.06. Without independence this joint occupancy cannot be determined from marginal measurements.
Four N-glycan sites have marginal occupancies 0.9, 0.8, 0.4 and 0.2. What is the average number of occupied sites per protein?
The expected number is the sum of occupancies, 2.3. Multiplication would yield the all-four probability only under independence; the mean does not require independence.
A steady-state phosphorylation system contains 5 µM protein, 40% modified, with k_add = 0.2 min⁻¹. What is its forward ATP consumption flux under one ATP per event?
0.4 µM/min
1.0 µM/min
0.6 µM/min
2.0 µM/min
Unmodified concentration is 5 × 0.6 = 3 µM; flux is 0.2 × 3 = 0.6 µM/min. The modified fraction is used for reverse flux, not forward flux.
A precursor converts irreversibly with a six-minute half-time. Starting with 64 nM precursor and no mature product, what mature concentration appears after 18 min if no degradation occurs?
8 nM
16 nM
32 nM
56 nM
Three half-times leave 64/8 = 8 nM precursor. The one-to-one mature product concentration is 64 − 8 = 56 nM.
Twenty pmol of sites are monomethylated. How much SAM is required to convert all to trimethylated sites with no reverse or competing reactions?
20 pmol
40 pmol
60 pmol
80 pmol
Each site requires two additional methyl transfers; 20 × 2 = 40 pmol. The first methyl group has already been installed.
A total-protein signal decreases from 100 to 50 calibrated units and phosphosite signal from 40 to 20 units, with comparable proportionality. What does the ratio show?
Occupancy unchanged
Occupancy doubles
Occupancy halves
Kinase activity necessarily rises
The normalized signal is 40/100 = 20/50 = 0.4. Absolute modified abundance decreased but fractional occupancy appears unchanged; kinase activity is not directly inferred.
A phosphatase treatment eliminates a phospho-specific band while total target remains unchanged. What is most directly supported?
The protein has been degraded
The antibody detects a phosphatase-sensitive state
The target must be N-glycosylated
The upstream kinase is identified
The result supports dependence of the detected epitope on phosphate. It neither identifies the kinase nor demonstrates degradation; other assay controls are still important.
Wild-type receptor recruits a partner after stimulation; Y→F mutant fails. Both reach the membrane. Which additional evidence best supports direct phosphotyrosine recognition?
More receptor mRNA
Equal cell sizes
Binding to a phosphorylated peptide but not its unmodified counterpart
Loss of an unrelated glycan
Matched peptides directly test dependence on the chemical mark. Equal localization already reduces one alternative explanation; mRNA and unrelated glycan changes do not establish direct recognition.
A cytosolic reporter with Asn-Ala-Ser is not glycosylated. Adding an ER signal peptide enables PNGase F-sensitive glycosylation. What is supported?
Asn motif requires ATP binding
The reporter changed its genetic code
The original reporter was a GPI-anchored protein
Access to the secretory compartment is important
The motif existed in both forms, but signal-dependent entry provides access to luminal OST. The result is consistent with conventional N-glycosylation, not a genetic-code change.
An early pulse-labeled protein is Endo H-sensitive; a later form is resistant but PNGase F-sensitive. What is the strongest conclusion?
The protein has acquired a different processed N-glycan state
The protein has no carbohydrate
Every molecule is definitively at the plasma membrane
The polypeptide has been phosphorylated
The differential glycosidase susceptibility supports N-glycan maturation. It does not identify the exact location of every protein or prove phosphorylation.
Tunicamycin reduces secretion of a glycoprotein. Which follow-up best distinguishes loss of a particular glycan from global ER stress?
Measure only drug concentration
Compare a site-specific mutant and assess folding, abundance and secretion
Assume all mRNA is destroyed
Count total ribosomes only
The site-specific mutation and multiple readouts address a direct glycan role versus widespread perturbation. The inhibitor alone affects numerous substrates and may induce stress.
A glycoprotein lacking its N-glycan is equally active in purified form but poorly secreted. Which interpretation is most plausible?
The glycan is essential to peptide-bond formation
The glycan must directly constitute the active site
The glycan may influence folding/transport or stability in the cell
The glycan must be a DNA modification

Intrinsic activity is preserved in the purified population, so a cellular role in processing, trafficking or stability is plausible. Additional localization and turnover data would distinguish those mechanisms.
After OGA inhibition an intracellular Ser/Thr-linked sugar increases, while total target is constant. What is most directly consistent?
Reduced removal of O-GlcNAc
Increased OST-mediated transfer of fourteen sugars
Removal of every phosphate from the target
Decreased protein synthesis necessarily
OGA removes O-GlcNAc, so inhibition can increase occupancy. Other marks and synthesis need independent measurement; the ER precursor transfer is a distinct mechanism.
A K→Q mutant behaves like an acetylated form in one binding assay. What conclusion is justified?
K→Q is chemically identical to acetyllysine
The mutant can be dynamically acetylated at Q
The target has no other modification sites
The neutral substitution supports a model but does not prove the native mark
Glutamine approximates neutralization but differs in length and chemistry. Direct measurement using the genuinely acetylated substrate is stronger.
A 42 Da nominal increase is found on a lysine-containing peptide. What is the best next step?
Call it phosphorylation
Use accurate mass, fragmentation and independent evidence
Call it glycosylation
Assume it is acetylation with certainty
Acetylation and trimethylation have similar nominal increments but different exact masses and chemical structures. Precursor nominal mass alone is insufficient.
A cytosolic signaling protein becomes soluble after mutating its N-terminal Gly. Which control best supports a myristoylation-dependent mechanism?
Measure unrelated histone acetylation
Assume no folding defect
Confirm loss of lipid label and compare total protein and fraction markers
Remove all membrane proteins
Direct lipid evidence plus fraction purity and abundance controls addresses anchoring. Mutation may otherwise disrupt structure or a distinct interaction.
An extracellular phospholipase releases a cell-surface protein, but a transmembrane control is retained. Which modification is consistent with the observation?
GPI attachment
Cytosolic prenylation
Nuclear methylation
Ribosomal phosphorylation
A susceptible GPI anchor can be cleaved from the extracellular side. Cytosolic lipid modifications are inaccessible to extracellular enzyme across an intact bilayer.
A precursor and its cleavage-resistant mutant accumulate equally. The mutant is inactive even with activating protease. What follow-up separates defective cleavage from catalytic misfolding?
Measure unrelated kinase
Add SAM to both
Measure only mRNA
Test a correctly engineered mature mutant form and folding

If a mature version bypassing cleavage is active and correctly folded, the activation defect is better explained by failed processing. Equal precursor abundance alone does not establish correct folding.
A pulse-chase shows disappearance of precursor label but no mature label. Which conclusion is warranted?
Complete maturation has been demonstrated
Disappearance alone cannot distinguish processing from loss
Every precursor has become phosphorylated
All protein synthesis has stopped
The labeled precursor may be degraded, exported, or otherwise lost. Detection and accounting of the expected mature species are necessary to establish conversion.
A protein accumulates with reduced ubiquitin tag after deletion of its ligase. A proteasome inhibitor instead causes accumulation of tagged protein. What is consistent with both?
The ligase removes every glycan
Proteasomes synthesize the ubiquitin tag
Tagging can precede degradation of this target
All ubiquitination necessarily has the same outcome
The two perturbations affect distinct steps: tagging versus destruction. The result supports a degradative tag for this particular substrate, not all ubiquitin marks.

A membrane receptor has a lumen-facing Asn-X-Thr motif and a cytosolic Tyr. The Asn mutation changes secretion, the Tyr mutation changes stimulated binding without changing surface abundance. What model fits?
Separate glycan-dependent maturation and phosphate-dependent recruitment mechanisms
Both sites are necessarily modified by the same enzyme
The cytosolic Tyr receives the canonical fourteen-sugar N-glycan
The receptor is synthesized by separate ribosomes for each domain

Topology and phenotypes fit distinct modification systems. An Asn-linked luminal glycan may influence processing, while a cytosolic phosphotyrosine can alter recruitment. Direct mark measurements would strengthen the model.
